name: Catalan's constant
rephrased: Catalan's constant is the sum of the alternating series 1 - 1/3² + 1/5² - 1/7² + ...
implication_form: Not applicable (this is a definition, not a conjecture to be proven)
explained: Catalan's constant (G) is a fundamental mathematical constant, approximately 0.9159656, defined as the infinite alternating sum of reciprocals of odd squares: \(1- rac{1}{3^{2}}+ rac{1}{5^{2}}- rac{1}{7^{2}}+\dots \), appearing in combinatorics, number theory, and geometry. It's named after Eugène Charles Catalan, and a major unsolved problem is whether it's rational or irrational, though it's strongly believed to be irrational.
subjects:
['Combinatorics': 'Counting domino tilings, spanning trees', 
'Geometry': 'Related to the volume of ideal hyperbolic polyhedra (e.g., 1/4 the volume of an ideal hyperbolic octahedron)',
